panel_first_index: Building the index, this only happens once...
panel_no_attribution: No local transcripts cover this window.
panel_hint_curve: Bars are the weighted cost of a turn, the line is how large the context was. They climb together: the same work costs a multiple once the conversation is long, and a compaction drops both back to the floor.
panel_hint_quota: The percentage is the one the API reports. The breakdown under it is local: sessions whose turns fall inside that window, ranked by weighted cost.
panel_weights_note: Weighted = input x1 + cache write x1.25 + cache read x0.1 + output x5
panel_hint_drag: Drag a card by its handle to reorder the charts. The order is remembered on this machine.
panel_hint_insights: Approximate, from the transcripts on this machine - it does not include other devices or claude.ai. These are independent characteristics of your usage, not a breakdown: one session can be all three.
panel_trait_context: of your cost was spent at a context above 150k
panel_advice_context: A long session is cheaper per token thanks to the cache, not cheap: the whole context is re-read every turn. Compact mid-task, clear when you switch to a new one.
panel_trait_subagents: of your cost came from sessions that were mostly subagents
panel_advice_subagents: Each subagent pays for its own context from scratch and shares no cache with the conversation that spawned it. Spawn them deliberately, and consider a cheaper model for the simple ones.
panel_trait_long: of your cost came from sessions open for 8 hours or more
panel_advice_long: Usually a loop or a background session nobody closed. Continuous usage adds up quietly - make sure it is intentional.
panel_on_top: Keep on top of other windows
